items.title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million. He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).

items.title: Trial by social media must cease
items.summary: LETTERS: Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has been charged in court for causing hurt and proceedings have yet to commence. It is extremely perturbing this incident has to be ventilated in court as it involves essential enforcement agencies of the government and the possibility of revealing how covert operations, intelligence, evidence from observation, deployment, instructions, are carried out as it will to some extent, become public knowledge. Although the matter is a summons case and can be compounded, it carries far reaching implications in all the careers and personal impact in the respective parties background in their respective agencies.

items.title: MACC seeks 24-year-old man to assist Sabah corruption probe, last traced to Semporna
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in an investigation in Sabah. In a statement today, MACC identified the man as Jamaluddin Jamahali, 24, who is being investigated under Section 17(b) of the MACC Act 2009. Anyone who knows his whereabouts or has relevant information is urged to contact investigating officer Abu Hudzaifah Abd Talib at 014-8573727 or via email at hudzaifah@sprm.gov.my.

items.title: 6 cases of illegal racing detected in KL operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six cases of illegal racing and speed testing were detected during an overnight enforcement operation in Kuala Lumpur, with nine motorcycles seized Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (RTD) director Hamidi Adam said the operation, conducted jointly with the department's Putrajaya headquarters, targeted illegal racing and dangerous riding along Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Ampang and the city centre. Hamidi said 35 vehicles were inspected during the seven-hour operation, with enforcement action taken against 11. "Nine motorcycles were also seized," he said.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for open tender to develop local Waze alternative
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should hold an open tender to develop a local road navigation app as an alternative to Waze, following criticism of TuJu's performance. "The government should open a tender so that capable local companies, especially those owned by young people, have a fair opportunity to develop a better navigation app. Lim said the government should allow sufficient time to develop and test any alternative navigation app, ensuring it was reliable before being introduced to users.

items.title: Police to question content creator who entered Zalina Azman's house
items.summary: Shah Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the individual would be called in to explain his actions. Sarudin said investigations into Zalina's disappearance were ongoing, but there were still no strong leads to warrant further action. "However, there are still no strong leads concerning the woman's disappearance," he said.

items.title: Experts warn against blanket Waze ban without consultation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consult industry experts before deciding whether to ban Waze, as a blanket ban could create problems for users and drivers. He said other applications, including WhatsApp and Instagram, also collected location information and personal data, raising similar concerns. Fong said applications could collect data beyond location information, including access to users' contact lists, cameras, microphones and photo galleries.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker disappointed Takiyuddin made mediation proposal public before his response
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul is disappointed with Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan's (PN-Kota Baru) decision to make his mediation proposal public without waiting for a response from him. Johari said he had earlier given Takiyuddin until last Thursday to withdraw his remark involving the word "munafik", following a complaint by RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong). Johari said Takiyuddin then sent him a letter stating that he was unwilling to withdraw the remark and proposing mediation involving the Speaker, Rayer and himself.

items.title: Langkawi duty-free status not meant to help the rich avoid luxury car taxes
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices. Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted. Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.

items.title: Women must shape media narratives, says NST editor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Women should have the power to shape how the world is portrayed, not merely appear in it, said New Straits Times Life & Times editor Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal. "Representation isn't simply about seeing more women in the picture; it's about giving women the power to help shape the picture," she said. Intan was speaking on "Women, Media and the Power of Representation: Shaping Inclusive Cities" at a plenary forum on catalysts for peace, dialogue and social cohesion at the third Southeast Asia Dialogue Cities Conference.

items.title: Zahid rejects RM2.1b overspending claims, says ministry underspent revised allocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today dismissed claims that his ministry overspent by RM2.1 billion, saying the figure reflected the difference between its original allocation and revised spending ceiling over three years. Winding up the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat, Zahid said the ministry spent RM6.108 billion between 2023 and 2025, against a revised allocation of RM6.143 billion after additional funding was approved, Free Malaysia Today reported. According to Johan, spending on rural road projects reached RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 compared with RM1.3 billion allocated, and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion approved.

items.title: Azalina: Malaysia studies models for proposed Law Reform Commission
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying suitable models for a proposed Malaysian Law Reform Commission that aligns with the country's legal and administrative framework, Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said. Azalina said the proposed commission will also conduct research and comparative studies, carry out public consultations, and independently recommend legal reforms, including assisting in drafting bills for government consideration. Azalina said the study will be followed by consultations with ministries, government agencies, legal practitioners, academics, and civil society.

items.title: 609 locations in Kelantan identified as flood-prone ahead of Northeast monsoon
items.summary: Siti Fairus said development and changes in land use could also increase surface runoff, causing water to flow more rapidly into low-lying areas. She said the federal government's Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin Development Project (PLSB), covering Phases 1, 2 and 3 for RM3.044 billion, was expected to improve drainage capacity and reduce flood risks in the rapidly developing areas of Pasir Mas and Tumpat. "Phase 3 is expected to reduce flood-risk areas by 15,000ha and protect 16,000 residents," she said.

items.title: Langkawi’s duty-free overhaul: RM300,000 vehicle price cap and RM10,000 spending limit
items.summary: Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said changes to the duty and tax exemption policy for vehicles were introduced not only to address revenue leakage but also to discourage such business practices. Liew acknowledged that some business operators would be affected by the policy but stressed that local residents would not be impacted. Earlier, he said that, effective Jan 1, 2026, duty and tax exemptions for vehicles would be capped at a value of RM300,000 to prevent wealthy individuals from abusing the incentives to acquire luxury vehicles.

items.title: Perkeso to provide rehabilitation aids to 2 journalists injured in Ipoh crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) will provide rehabilitation aids to two female media practitioners injured in an accident in Menglembu, Ipoh, early yesterday morning to support their recovery. In a statement today, Perkeso said the incident was classified as an employment injury as they were travelling for an official assignment and both were covered under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 under the Lindung Pekerja scheme. She has been given one month of medical leave and Perkeso will provide her with suitable rehabilitation aids upon receiving the medical report from her doctor.

items.title: Zahid explains RM2.1bil overspending on rural development projects
items.summary: Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the figure was derived by comparing actual expenditure of RM6.108 billion with the original allocation of RM3.982 billion, without taking into account the revised allocation. It was derived by subtracting the original allocation of RM3.982 billion from actual expenditure of RM6.108 billion, without taking into account the revised allocation. He said the programme's financial position should be assessed by distinguishing between the original allocation, revised allocation and actual expenditure, rather than comparing spending with the original allocation alone.

items.title: SKA Capital unit secures RM89.28mil contracts for TNB projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SKA Capital Bhd's subsidiary, SKA Rekabina Sdn Bhd, has secured six contracts worth RM89.28 million from Ibrahim & Sons Sdn Bhd for Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) projects. They also include underground cable laying and jointing works for TNB's distribution network in Selangor. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ramkarpal: Time to review death penalty for non-murder offences
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia should consider abolishing the death penalty for offences other than murder, following legal reforms introduced since 2023, says Bukit Gelugor MP Ramkarpal Singh. The former deputy minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said the proposal could secure bipartisan support in parliament, given developments following the abolition of mandatory death sentences three years ago. "I believe there is bipartisan support for abolishing the death penalty for offences other than murder.

items.title: Madani govt resolves 12 MA63 matters, highest under any administration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani government has resolved 12 matters under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), the highest number settled by any administration. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the achievement reflected the government's efforts to address long-standing issues that had remained under negotiation for years. "Twelve matters have been resolved, while previous administrations settled only four.

items.title: Malaysia to benefit from cross-border electricity project with Vietnam, Singapore
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Malaysia stands to benefit from a cross-border electricity project involving Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) through local contractor participation, engineering expertise and the development of renewable energy certificate mechanisms, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof. Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation minister, said the project, involving the purchase of offshore wind energy from Vietnam and its transmission to Singapore, would create opportunities for Malaysian contractors to participate in the development of transmission infrastructure, including undersea cables. Fadillah said Malaysia could also contribute its expertise in developing a mechanism for exchanging renewable energy certificates with Vietnam, which he said was crucial to the project's commercial viability.

items.title: Haze eases as Northeast Monsoon set to begin
items.summary: The Malaysian Meteorological Department said the Northeast Monsoon, which begins tomorrow, would stop transboundary haze from drifting into Malaysia. Its director-general, Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, said continuous northeasterly winds would keep transboundary haze away. Hisham said wet weather was expected in most areas this week.

items.title: Pakatan ties, Perikatan disciplinary action on agenda at Bersatu meeting tonight
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Bersatu’s supreme leadership council is set to meet tonight to finalise, among other matters, the party’s political cooperation plans ahead of the 16th Melaka state election. As reported by Harian Metro , the meeting, chaired by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, is understood to begin at 8pm at the party’s headquarters in Petaling Jaya. Bersatu has recently been linked to a possible electoral cooperation pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls.

items.title: Son takes on BN stronghold after father's five election defeats
items.summary: His father, Julasapiyah Kassim, first contested the Kuala Linggi seat in 1999. "The people's trust is something I must earn and prove for myself," he said when contacted today. "Young people today are leaders of the present.

items.title: Flight attendant charged over drunk driving crash that killed DBKL road crew on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A flight attendant pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here today to two charges of driving under the influence of alcohol, causing the death of a supervisor and injuring a lorry driver in an accident on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar here on Saturday (Oct 24). Mohd Iman Nafiz Fong Mohd Sabirin, 26, is accused of driving with a blood alcohol concentration of 64 milligrams (mg) per 100 millilitres (ml) of blood, exceeding the legal limit of 50mg per 100ml, and causing the death of Faris Irfan Fazli, 29, on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar heading towards Jalan Parlimen at 4.09 am on Oct 24. If convicted, the accused may also be disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence for a period of at least 10 years from the date of conviction.

items.title: British policeman drives, collects and celebrates classic Protons
items.summary: Jon Coupland, who lives in Boston, Lincolnshire, said he was drawn to the distinctive designs of older Proton models, which have become increasingly rare in the UK. "I realised Proton models had their own charm, but were increasingly being forgotten in the UK. His first purchase was a 1990 Proton Saga 1.5 SE LE UK Special Edition, which cost £700 (about RM4,000).

items.title: DAP contests seven Melaka seats based on winning chances, says Loke
items.summary: MELAKA: DAP's decision to contest only seven seats in the 16th Melaka election was based on an assessment of its winning chances, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said. He said the decision took into account the party's performance in the 2021 state election, when DAP finished second in several seats it lost, but placed third in Bemban. That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time.

items.title: High Court allows 12 Ampang Jaya residents to challenge local plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court's decision to grant 12 Ampang Jaya residents leave to challenge the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) through judicial review marks a significant step in their bid to protect community interests. In a statement, residents' action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed the plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws, including land-use changes that had not been made public. The group also alleged that objections raised during a public hearing in 2022 had not been incorporated into the plan.

items.title: Sepang eyes F1 return with Cabinet proposal due in November
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is drafting a feasibility study on bringing back the Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) to Malaysia, to be presented to the Cabinet in November. SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said it was currently holding engagement sessions with the government, relevant agencies and industry players to obtain accurate information and data for inclusion in the study. He said the findings would serve as one of the factors for the government to consider before deciding whether Malaysia should return as host of the prestigious race.

items.title: Australia's Ingenia hits 9-month high on AVID's US$1.5bil buyout bid
items.summary: AUSTRALIA: Ingenia Communities Group received a takeover proposal from AVID Property Group for A$2.2 billion (US$1.54 billion), sending the Australian property developer's shares to their highest close in nine months. Ingenia, which develops and operates communities offering rental and holiday accommodation, has already received three bids from Warburg Pincus, sending its shares up more than 35 per cent since the first offer in September. Last week, Ingenia set an October 23 deadline to sign a process deed with Warburg Pincus.

items.title: Indonesia extends share buyback policy until June 2027 amid market volatility
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) has extended a policy allowing listed companies to buy back their own shares without shareholder approval until June 2027, amid efforts to strengthen market stability following a sharp stock market sell-off. Meanwhile, Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) president director Jeffrey Hendrik said global index provider FTSE Russell had reaffirmed Indonesia's classification as a Secondary Emerging Market during an online meeting on Oct 23, following discussions on reforms covering transparency, liquidity and market surveillance. "FTSE Russell confirmed that its Oct 6 report clearly maintained Indonesia's classification as a Secondary Emerging Market.

items.title: Driver fined after viral video shows two men sitting on moving car roof
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have issued summonses to a driver after a viral video showed two men sitting on the roof of his moving car in Taman Puteri Wangsa, Ulu Tiram. "The driver, who was traced on Oct 25, was found to have been driving without insurance coverage or a valid driving licence," he said in a statement. The summonses were issued under Sections 47, 26 and 23 of the Road Transport Act 1987 for carrying passengers in a dangerous manner, driving without insurance coverage and driving without a valid licence, respectively.

items.title: KPKT moves to standardise short-term rental accommodation rules nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), through PLANMalaysia and in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (MOTAC), state governments and local authorities, is drafting STRA planning guidelines to serve as a uniform source of authority. The move comes as the government seeks to require that only premises registered and fully compliant with local authority licensing conditions may legally operate short-term rental accommodation (STRA) nationwide, said Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu. Aiman Athirah said digital platform providers must take responsibility for delisting premises that are unlicensed or in breach of local authority conditions and existing laws, while enforcement agencies hold the legal power to act firmly against recalcitrant operators.

items.title: Melaka polls: DAP skips Bemban due to slim chances of winning, says Loke
items.summary: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the decision was made on strategic grounds to ensure the party could focus its machinery, resources and attention on seven seats where it stood a better chance of winning. He said DAP assessed each seat based on its chances of winning rather than simply considering the party's traditional position in a particular constituency. He said Bemban was the only seat contested by DAP in the previous election where the party finished third, while it came second in the other seats it failed to win.

items.title: Malaysia's private hospitals enter a new expansion cycle amid rising demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's private hospital operators are embarking on a new expansion cycle, driven by existing hospital expansions, acquisitions and new developments, as healthcare groups seek to capture growing demand. Maybank Investment Bank (Maybank IB) said new private hospital investments remained concentrated in established healthcare markets, namely the Klang Valley, Penang, Johor and Melaka. Its Thomson Hospital Kota Damansara currently has 399 operational beds, against a total capacity of 554 beds, while its proposed 500-bed Thomson Hospital Iskandariah in Johor Baru is targeted for completion in 2030.

items.title: TNB, Petronas-backed regional power project secures Singapore's conditional approval
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) are moving closer to developing a regional renewable electricity corridor linking Vietnam, Malaysia and Singapore, following conditional approval from Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The approval was granted to Sembcorp Utilities Pte Ltd, a subsidiary of Singapore-listed Sembcorp Industries, for a project that aims to supply Singapore with up to 1.3 gigawatts of renewable electricity through the Vietnam-Malaysia-Singapore initiative. The approval follows a joint development agreement signed in May 2025 between three parties: PetroVietnam Technical Services Corp, a member of Vietnam National Industry–Energy Group; Sembcorp Utilities, the project's designated electricity importer; and MY Energy Consortium, comprising TNB and Petronas.

items.title: Pahang exports hit RM10.95bil in first eight months, signalling growth potential
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang recorded RM10.95 billion in exports in the first eight months of this year, highlighting the state's potential for further growth. Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) chief executive officer Datuk Abu Bakar Yusof said the state remained resilient, supported by strong economic fundamentals and promising growth prospects. "These figures present opportunities to diversify Pahang's export base and enable more local entrepreneurs to participate in international trade," he said at the 2026 Pahang Export Day.

items.title: Arroyo: Malaysia's reforms could pave way for death penalty abolition
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Ex-Philippine president Gloria Arroyo said Malaysia's move to abolish the mandatory death penalty could pave the way for full abolition. Replacing death sentences with other penalties, imposing a moratorium on executions and abolishing the mandatory death penalty could lay the groundwork for wider reform, she said. Replacing death sentences with other penalties, a moratorium and the abolition of the mandatory death penalty, as Malaysia has so courageously done, can change the landscape and pave the way for the full abolition of the death penalty," she said.

items.title: Loke defends DAP’s seat reduction for Melaka poll as tactical shift for better odds
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — DAP’s decision to contest only seven seats in the 16th Melaka state election, including its decision not to field a candidate in Bemban, was based on an assessment of its chances of winning, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said. He said the decision took into account DAP’s performance in the 2021 state election, when the party finished second in several seats it failed to win, but came third in Bemban. That is why we are contesting only seven seats this time.

items.title: Malaysia targets bankruptcy discharges in under 36 days next year
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the initiative under the Fast Track Discharge Programme would be implemented through the Malaysian Insolvency Department (MdI). Azalina said the government had also strengthened its recovery efforts through the Second Chance Policy, which recorded 253,457 bankruptcy discharges from 2023 to September 2026. Azalina said the digitalisation of MdI services also enabled bankruptcy discharge applications to be submitted online through the e-Insolvensi portal.

items.title: High Court dismisses ex-student’s RM400,000 suit over phone seizure during SPM trial exam
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court has upheld the dismissal of a RM400,000 negligence and defamation suit filed by a former student against her teachers and the government over a body search and the seizure of her mobile phone during an SPM trial examination six years ago. The court ruled that while the school was entitled to confiscate Nabilah’s mobile phone, it had no authority under Education Ministry guidelines or school examination regulations to inspect its contents. Checks on the phone uncovered notes, examination questions and answer schemes for several subjects.

items.title: Major legal win for Ampang Jaya residents as court allows challenge to council’s development plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The High Court’s decision to grant leave to 12 Ampang Jaya residents to initiate judicial review proceedings challenging the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Local Plan 2035 (RT MPAJ 2035) marked a significant step forward for local community rights. In a statement, residents’ action group TOLAK RT2035 claimed that the local plan, gazetted on Feb 6, 2025, contained fundamental flaws and unpublicised land-use conversions. They further claimed that the local plan did not incorporate the objections raised during the 2022 public objection hearing.

items.title: Pensioner charged in Kangar with sexual assault, using criminal force against two preteen girls
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 26 — A government retiree pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to three charges of committing physical sexual assault and criminal force against two girls about two months ago. The first two charges alleged that Annuar committed physical sexual assault for sexual purposes against an 11-year-and-five-month-old girl at a house at No. The first two charges were brought under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.

items.title: Dr Mahathir absent from SG4 forum due to health issues, Mokhzani reads keynote
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was unable to attend the SG4 Business and Economic Forum 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today due to health reasons. His son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, said the 101-year-old statesman had prepared his keynote speech and intended to deliver it himself, but had been feeling unwell in recent weeks, Berita Harian (BH) reported. Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir was also present.

items.title: Dr Akmal Saleh willing to sit out Melaka polls if court case hurts BN chances
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 26 — Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh says he is prepared to give up his bid to defend the Merlimau state seat in the Melaka election on November 14 if the court case he faces hurts Umno and Barisan Nasional’s chances at the polls. According to Berita Harian , Dr Akmal said he had conveyed his position to Barisan Nasional chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, stressing that the party’s interests must come before his personal ambitions. The 38-year-old said Umno had entrusted him with defending the Merlimau seat, although the final decision would only be known on nomination day.

items.title: AKPS rolls out hologram technology to help travellers navigate arrival procedures
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 26 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has developed hologram technology to be deployed at the satellite building of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, to assist travellers in obtaining information regarding arrival procedures in the country. He noted that the development of this hologram was inspired by an initiative from the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), which installed a hologram of the Minister of Home Affairs, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex. “Just as the Ministry of Home Affairs placed a hologram of the Minister in the lobby of the Setia Perkasa Complex, AKPS shares the same vision and mission.

items.title: Orang Asli in remote Kelantan and Terengganu areas urged to evacuate early as monsoon looms
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Oct 26 — Orang Asli living in remote areas have been urged to move to safe locations immediately if faced with the threat of floods, sudden torrents or landslides during the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), without waiting for conditions to become critical. Kelantan and Terengganu Orang Asli Development Department (JAKOA) director Mohd Faedzyal Mohamed said all Tok Batin (Orang Asli village heads), penghulu (sub-district chiefs) and Orang Asli Village Development and Security Committees had been instructed to step up preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year. Mohd Faedzyal said village leaders needed to identify high-risk areas, monitor weather changes and river levels, and identify residents who might require immediate assistance during emergencies.

items.title: Former Court of Appeal judge Mahadev Shankar dies at 94, leaves enduring legal legacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Former Court of Appeal Judge Datuk Mahadev Shankar, renowned for his legal acumen, language mastery, and enduring contributions to Malaysian jurisprudence, died at Shah Alam Hospital at 2 am today. His close friend, Malaysia-India Heritage Society founder-president Prabhakaran Nair, said funeral arrangements would be announced later. Mahadev was also recognised for his contributions to legal scholarship.

items.title: Lynas waste disposal facility reaches 77pc completion as 2031 deadline looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The permanent disposal facility (PDF) for radioactive waste generated by Lynas Malaysia Sdn Bhd had achieved 77 per cent completion in construction and operations as of Aug 31, with 1.45 million metric tonnes of the 1.467 million metric tonnes of Water Leach Purification (WLP) waste generated having been transferred to the facility. Chang said Lynas was required to stop generating WLP radioactive waste before March 2031, while existing waste and waste generated during the period must be treated to reduce its activity concentration to below one becquerel (Bq) per gram using methods proven effective through research and development (R&D). After the five years, if Lynas is still generating radioactive WLP waste, the JTA may suspend or revoke the licence.

items.title: Loke says RM1,000 driver aid not a Melaka poll sweetener, rollout continues nationwide
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook has denied that the RM1,000 special financial assistance given to taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Melaka today was intended to fish for votes ahead of the Melaka state election. “I am distributing the assistance in Melaka today. Taxi and rental car drivers in every state nationwide will receive this assistance,” he said.

items.title: Dr Akmal Saleh’s lawyers to file second representation after prosecutors reject bid to drop charge
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 26 — Prosecutors have rejected a representation by Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh seeking to have a charge against him dropped, prompting his lawyers to submit a second appeal to the Attorney General. His lead counsel, Aizat Azam, said the defence has applied to file a second representation to the Attorney General, setting out the facts and legal arguments relating to the case, Sinar Harian ( SH ) reported. Speaking outside the Bukit Mertajam Court Complex today, Aizat said the first representation, filed in December 2025, was rejected and the decision conveyed during today’s case mention.

items.title: ‘No compromise’: Selangor exco backs police probe into drug stash at Klang temple
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 26 — The Selangor state government will not tolerate the use of any place of worship for criminal purposes, regardless of the religion, race or background of those involved. Selangor Human Resources and Poverty Eradication Committee chairman V. Papparaidu said he took seriously media reports about drugs being found at an unregistered place of worship in Klang during an operation by the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department from Oct 13 to 19. “Places of worship should be respected, kept sacred and provide peace to their respective congregations, not be used to store prohibited substances or facilitate criminal activities,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: MoHE urges off-campus students to report residential addresses for monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — The Higher Education Ministry (MoHE) has stressed that students living in rented accommodation off campus should inform their universities of their place of residence to facilitate monitoring. Its minister, Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, said monitoring was difficult because some students arranged their own rental accommodation without going through their universities. Zambry said some public universities and polytechnics worked with their student affairs divisions to manage accommodation in designated areas, while some students opted to rent accommodation independently.

items.title: Anwar calls for service over rhetoric as Pakatan targets Melaka victory
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged all candidates and party machinery to work hard to earn the people’s trust in the 16th Melaka state election. “Come, all Pakatan Harapan candidates and machinery uphold the trust placed in you for the Melaka state election through hard work. PH is fielding 21 candidates from its three component parties for the 16th Melaka state election, compared to 28 candidates in 2021.

items.title: Seventeen people narrowly escape as massive fire guts homes in Seremban
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 26 — Four semi-permanent houses located behind UTC Ampangan here was 80 per cent destroyed in a fire tonight. Seremban Fire and Rescue Station Senior Fire Officer I Raihan Che Mat said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 8.17 pm. The operation involves personnel from Seremban station with assistance from Ampangan and Seremban 2 stations,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Three dead after MPV collides with TNB vehicle on Terengganu trunk road
items.summary: Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received information about the crash at 5.15 pm involving a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) and a Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) four-wheel-drive vehicle. He said the third victim, Mohamad Zulkefli’s younger brother, Muhammad Alif Syukri Ishak, 18, died around 7 pm while receiving treatment at Dungun Hospital. Nik Ab Halim said the two occupants of the four-wheel-drive vehicle, Mohamad Syafiq Nasrullah Said, 39, and Muhammad Fadhlan Abd Manan, 32, sustained minor injuries.

items.title: Anwar congratulates ‘dear friend’ Lula on Brazil election triumph
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today congratulated Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his election victory, saying Malaysia looked forward to strengthening ties with the South American nation under his continued leadership. The prime minister said Malaysia was keen to expand cooperation with Brazil in trade and investment, strengthen engagement between Asean and Latin America, and deepen bilateral ties. “Malaysia looks forward to working closely with Brazil under President Lula’s continued leadership.

items.title: Win first, settle after: Zambry tells BN parties to focus on Melaka race
items.summary: LUMUT, Oct 26 — All parties in Barisan Nasional (BN) must prioritise securing victory for the coalition in the 16th Melaka state election rather than dwelling on differences over seat allocations. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said all component parties should focus on winning the 21 seats allocated to BN, in line with the consensus reached. On Saturday, Bernama reported that MCA would not recognise any of its members announced as BN candidates for the Melaka state election without the approval of the party’s top leadership.

items.title: Two Hong Kong cocaine arrests linked to Penang as police reveal details of first case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A Chinese national arrested in Hong Kong last week with 2kg of suspected cocaine is believed to have obtained the drugs from an unidentified individual at a supermarket in Penang, police said today. According to Berita Harian (BH), Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the preliminary finding emerged following the arrest of the 25-year-old man by Hong Kong Customs and Excise on October 22. The suspect had arrived in Hong Kong from Penang on a Cathay Pacific flight when customs officers allegedly discovered the suspected cocaine in his checked luggage.

items.title: KLIA quarters murder: Man charged with killing his AKPS wife
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 26 — A man was charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with murdering his wife, an officer with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters on Oct 15. Mohd Khairudin Safi’ai, 37, nodded to indicate he understood the charge read before Magistrate Nurul Saqinah Rosli. Mohd Khairudin is accused of murdering Norhazwani Ibrahim, 35, at a house in the KLIA Civil Servants’ Housing Complex in Nilai at about 7 pm on Oct 15.

items.title: Police warn public to avoid Bagan Lalang Beach after crocodile sighting
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — Visitors and tourists have been urged to stay away from Bagan Lalang Beach after reports of a crocodile sighting near the popular coastal area. According to Berita Harian , Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said police received reports from members of the public late yesterday afternoon of a suspected crocodile being sighted near the beach. He said the animal was reported near a resort in Sungai Pelek.
